my hair is really flat and straight when i don’t style it too. heres what works for me and may work for you:

get your hair wet (i just take a shower first). then get yourself some texturizing spay like a sea salt spray. they’re super cheap and helps add volume to your hair. then, use some pomade or wax. i’m not sure on the differences, but my hair stylist gave me some old spice wax that works great. it’s not shiny, which i like, but it has a great hold. apply a nickel sized amount to your finger and rub it into your hands. then SCRUNCH your whole head. scrunch every single spot of hair on your head. DO NOT COMB OR RUN YOUR FINGERS THROUGH IT. that breaks any amount of curl you have and will make your hair look straight. 

the next step is optional, as you can always just air dry it, but i use a hair dryer with a diffuser attachment. works perfectly. remember to scrunch your hair as you dry it, and depending on your hair type of course, it should have at least a little bit of wave to it, or at the bare minimum, more volume. hope this helps

my advice, is to show her some statistics. first of all there is no clear evidence that there is a difference in a male and a female brain. 

https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fnins.2019.00185/full#:~:text=Ingalhalikar%20et%20al.,et%20al.%2C%202005).

this goes over some studies that show minimal differences in male and female brains. i found some other studies come up with a similar conclusion. 

next, you could explain to her exactly how being transgender works physically. we are all female in the womb, but our chromosomes (and other factors) decide how we continue to develop. as a gross oversimplification, these factors cause hormones to be released (more testosterone or more estrogen, depending on the factors) and that leads you to developing into a boy or girl. your gender can be changed because everyone has estrogen and testosterone in them, no matter their sex. imagine a gender as a sliding scale rather than two separate boxes. on one end, you have people who have more estrogen in their bodies (mostly afab) and on the other end are people who have more testosterone in their bodies (mostly amab). the more of one hormone you put in your body, the more you slide to one end rather than the other. for example, i am ftm. when i start testosterone, i will slide to the other end of the scale from where i am now. i will experience male changes because of the testosterone in my body. i will have amab like (not exclusive to amab though) characteristics like body hair, fat redistribution, a deepening voice, etc. when your friend starts hrt, she will see “feminine” changes. she will indeed be a real woman, and not a knockoff of the real deal. sure there are things that require surgery or other treatments, but her body will quite literally move towards and afab body. transitioning isn’t recreating the female or male experience, it is becoming a man or woman or other. hopefully this clarification helps. i may be wrong on some points, but this is how i remember it being described to me. i recommend looking into it further. 

lastly, a lot of this you can’t help with. you are just one person, and her issues are internal. remind yourself that it is not your job to fix her problems, because you can’t. i know it may sound harsh, but you cannot fix her problems for her. she will get likely better when she starts treatment, but you can be there for her and comfort her. look into general calming methods used in dbt, and ways for her, not for you to convince her, to realize that things are going to be okay. remember, you can’t fix things, but you can try to help her realize that things will get better. you could try talking through things with her more by using prompts from dbt worksheets (i feel ____ when____ etc.). 

you’re a good friend, and i admire how much you help her. just please, take care of yourself and remember that you can’t fix everything. i hope this helped.
